outcome: Detection and log search run over one data set again, with sources that were dropped for cost brought back within reach.
overview: Legacy security information platforms are usually replaced for one reason, and it is rarely a capability gap: the licence grew faster than the estate, and the team started dropping log sources to keep the renewal affordable. Falcon Next-Gen SIEM combines the log platform’s economics with detection content and the vendor’s own endpoint telemetry, which is already sitting in the tenant rather than integrated into it. The migration cost that gets underestimated every time is content: detection rules, dashboards and reports represent years of accumulated engineering, and moving them is the actual project rather than the platform build.

benefits.limits: The comparison must be against the incumbent’s actual renewal at equivalent source coverage, not against its list price

benefits.text: Endpoint telemetry already in the tenant is available to detection content without an integration
benefits.limits: This advantage applies to estates already on the vendor’s endpoint platform; without it the argument is a log platform argument alone

benefits.text: Detection, investigation and log search operate over one data set
benefits.limits: The platform is agent-and-cloud, so telemetry leaves the customer estate; the tenant region is a design decision to be made and recorded rather than a default to be accepted

residency: Log and detection data is held in the vendor tenant in a selected region, recorded at design

notFor.situation: A team with a heavily invested detection content library and no capacity to migrate it

notFor.situation: An estate not on this vendor’s endpoint platform
notFor.why: The telemetry advantage that differentiates this is absent
